library(PlayerPredictorMLB)

# Introduction

For this vignette, we will walk through a real use case that this package can
help with. We will be examining the post-deadline performance of Brett Bateman.
As much as I want to believe it was real, it was a small sample, and the
underlying numbers may not support what he did.

It didn't take long for Bateman to make his MLB debut after being acquired for
Kevin Gausman, and the 24-year-old outfielder appeared in 41 games. He quickly
made his mark, hitting .329/.402/.424 with 28 runs, 11 RBIs, and a 1.9 WAR.
Despite not being known for his power, he hit two home runs, including one at
Rogers Centre before Vladimir Guerrero Jr. was able to snap his drought. He
produced a 138 WRC+ and 6 DRS, showcasing excellent offensive and defensive
value. If that can be sustained over a full season, the Jays have a future star
on their hands, and it could be cool to see if the numbers support it!

## Finding Similar Batters

The first step to understand what Bateman accomplished is to find players that
profile as similar to him. Your first thought may be that with a small sample,
the projections wouldn't work, but all inputs of the function are rate stats.
They may be sensitive to the small samples, but Bateman only having 28 runs or
7 doubles won't be held against him.

To find similar players, what is needed are Bateman's stats from FanGraphs. You
need his BB%, K%, HR/FB rate, Barrel%, HardHit%, xBA, xSLG, and xwoBA. The
last piece is the number of similar player-seasons you want to see.

```{r}
similar_bateman <- similar_batters(
bb_pct = 9.9,
k_pct = 19.3,
hr_fb = 8.7,
barrel_pct = 1.6,
hardhit_pct = 19.8,
xba = 0.268,
xslg = 0.338,
xwoba = 0.312,
n = 10
)

similar_bateman
```

The results are not overly inspiring, but this is not surprising. Most light
hitters don't have the best success, and being compared to Nolan Schanuel and
Myles Straw is not exactly a glowing endorsement. That being said, there are a
lot of positives. We see 2024 Jake McCarthy and Brice Turang, both of who had
excellent 2026 seasons. Turang in particular, as he finished a distant third in
MVP voting, and both these guys are capable defenders like Bateman. 2025 Sal
Frelick, 2021 J.P. Crawford, and 2023 Ha-Seong Kim all had strong seasons as
well, giving us a nice range of potential outcomes for Bateman.

## WAR Calculator

The next step is to get an approximate value of what Brett Bateman's performance
would be worth. We can start with his two-month debut, as Bateman was worth 1.9
fWAR.

```{r}
bateman_war <- WAR_dollar_value_calculator(war = 1.9, seasons = 1)

bateman_war
```

$14,650,000 isn't too shabby for 41 games, as the young outfielder was worth
far more than his minimum value salary. It's unreasonable to expect a center
fielder to play a full 162 games, but 150 games is more realistic. At his 41
game pace, that would equate to an even 7 WAR.

```{r}
bateman_150_war <- WAR_dollar_value_calculator(war = 7, seasons = 1)

bateman_150_war
```

That's not quite PCA good, but if Bateman put up 7 WAR he'd be worth a whopping
$80.5 million -- far above the highest annual value for any MLB player. No team
would be willing to pay that, even for a Shohei Ohtani, and it's tough to expect
that production from a second-year player.

A better potential gauge of his value would be using the similar players, and we
can set a range for his production. To do so, I took the lowest WAR, Charlie
Blackmon's 0.1 in 2024, the highest WAR, Ha-Seong Kim's 4.2 in 2023, and the
total WAR of all 10 player-seasons, which can be summed and treated as a
player's 10-year career. That came out to 22.6.

```{r}
similar_low_war <- WAR_dollar_value_calculator(war = 0.1, seasons = 1)
similar_high_war <- WAR_dollar_value_calculator(war = 4.2, seasons = 1)
similar_total_war <- WAR_dollar_value_calculator(war = 22.6, seasons = 10)

similar_low_war
similar_high_war
similar_total_war
```

On the low end, a $700k season from Bateman next year would be a disappointment,
but the $44.1 million for a 4.2 WAR season would be considered a major win. Even
the average $18.88 million season value would be acceptable, and is very similar
to what Dalton Varsho produced in 2025. His 2.2 WAR was worth just a tad under
at $18.1 million, though it was injuries that held him to 71 games and not a
full season of production.

## Predicting 2027 Stats

The last thing to examine is what Bateman's 2025 performance says about his
projected performance in 2027. We can use his stats to predict his average,
slugging, and wOBA for 2027, with the model putting the most weight to the
corresponding xStat.

```{r}
bateman_avg <-predict_avg(
 age = 24,
 xba = 0.268,
 xslg = 0.338,
 xwoba = 0.312,
 bb_pct = 9.9,
 k_pct = 19.3,
 iso = 0.095,
 wrc_plus = 138,
 hr_fb = 8.7,
 barrel_pct = 1.6,
 hardhit_pct = 19.8
)

bateman_slg <-predict_slg(
 age = 24,
 xba = 0.268,
 xslg = 0.338,
 xwoba = 0.312,
 bb_pct = 9.9,
 k_pct = 19.3,
 iso = 0.095,
 wrc_plus = 138,
 hr_fb = 8.7,
 barrel_pct = 1.6,
 hardhit_pct = 19.8
)

bateman_woba <-predict_woba(
 age = 24,
 xba = 0.268,
 xslg = 0.338,
 xwoba = 0.312,
 bb_pct = 9.9,
 k_pct = 19.3,
 iso = 0.095,
 wrc_plus = 138,
 hr_fb = 8.7,
 barrel_pct = 1.6,
 hardhit_pct = 19.8
)

bateman_stats <-data.frame(
  AVG = bateman_avg,
  SLG = bateman_slg,
  wOBA = bateman_woba
)

bateman_stats

```

The models predicted that for Bateman in 2027 he would hit .266 with a .346
slugging and .308 wOBA, not the greatest overall production. It's not bad by
any means, especially paired with his defense, but it also makes sense. Bateman
slugged well over .400 despite a 1.6 Barrell% and 19.8 HardHit%. Those are both
well below average, and since few players can succeed with those metrics, it
makes sense that the models would not expect Bateman to produce a .329 average,
.424 slugging, and .368 wOBA, because batters like him don't usually do that.
And really no one hits .329!

## Future Exploration

This can be expanded upon using the newly predicted values. You can now find
similar players using the predicted average, slugging, and wOBA as the xBA,
xSLG, and see if that produces a different set of players. In most cases it
should be similar, but when analyzing different players they may have large
gaps between their season and the projections.

Further exploration can also be done on pitchers instead, as the package has
the ability to run a similar process on a pitcher. You can predict ERA and FIP,
as the functions account for the role the pitcher had or is expected to have.
Examples are provided with each function.

## Conclusion

As impressive as Brett Bateman's debut was, the tools in this package would not
expect him to do as impressive in a full season. That's not to say he would not
be valuable, as the ten most similar seasons produced an average of 2.26 WAR,
and two of the players with similar seasons in 2024 were outstanding in 2026.
Bateman could take a similar path, but regardless of if he keeps up this stellar
production, his combination of speed, defense, and contact ability will make him
an important piece for the 2027 Toronto Blue Jays.

As long as the MLB doesn't spoil it with an extended lockout...
